items.gist: The passage opens the clear display of the mandala and begins measuring the eastern field, brahman, and jiva regions.
It continues with brahman-side and jiva-side lunar segments, then draws sutras to establish the central peak.
It specifies the staff, outer gates, and the surrounding padma with jiva sutras.
It details petals, karṇika colors, pitha, horns, and the staff's coloration.
It describes the door's varied, ornate forms and its placement in the field.
It gives another measuring procedure for drawing lines, staff, and descending leaf-like forms.
It places lotuses and specifies colors for karṇika, petals, shula, and staff.
It identifies the deities worshipped in the shula and the four gross and subtle shaktis.
It names the rite as Damara and introduces the traishirasa shula-lotus procedure.
It begins the traishirasa construction with purification, central trishula, staff, and base measurements.
It specifies the vedi, half-moon forms, and the gandika's dimensions.
It details the gandika, shula tip, aram, and central hollow.
It adds petals, three cakras, and color applications for the shula.
It completes the construction with lotuses, sky-line, vedi, square wall, and gates.
